Real checks combine libraries. Run a process, **capture its output to a file**
with `stdout=<path>`, then read that file back with OperatingSystem and assert
on it. That is the pattern for verifying what a tool produced.

## Task 1 — Capture process output to a file and verify it

**Goal:** create `checks/combine.robot` that runs `tools/inventory.py list`,
captures its stdout to a file under `${OUTPUT_DIR}`, then reads that file back
and asserts a product name is in it.

Here is the same capture-then-verify flow over a different command. Adapt it.

<!-- example -->
```robotframework
*** Settings ***
Library    Process
Library    OperatingSystem

*** Test Cases ***
Save Version To A File
    ${result}=    Run Process    python3    --version    stdout=${OUTPUT_DIR}/version.txt
    Should Be Equal As Integers    ${result.rc}    0
    File Should Exist    ${OUTPUT_DIR}/version.txt
    ${text}=    Get File    ${OUTPUT_DIR}/version.txt
    Should Contain    ${text}    Python
```
<!-- /example -->

**Check:** the suite defines `Capture Inventory To A File`.

<!-- hint -->
Add `stdout=${OUTPUT_DIR}/inventory.txt` as a trailing cell on the
`Run Process    python3    tools/inventory.py    list` call to capture its output.
<!-- /hint -->
<!-- hint -->
After the run, `File Should Exist    ${OUTPUT_DIR}/inventory.txt`, then
`Get File` it and `Should Contain    ${captured}    Travel Mug`.
<!-- /hint -->
<!-- solution -->
```robotframework
*** Settings ***
Library    Process
Library    OperatingSystem

*** Test Cases ***
Capture Inventory To A File
    ${result}=    Run Process    python3    tools/inventory.py    list    stdout=${OUTPUT_DIR}/inventory.txt
    Should Be Equal As Integers    ${result.rc}    0
    File Should Exist    ${OUTPUT_DIR}/inventory.txt
    ${captured}=    Get File    ${OUTPUT_DIR}/inventory.txt
    Should Contain    ${captured}    Travel Mug
```
<!-- /solution -->

## Task 2 — Run it green

Run:

```bash
uv run robot checks
```

**Check:** the CLI output is captured to a file, then read and verified.
